paper.title: Are We Really Making Much Progress? A Worrying Analysis of Recent Neural Recommendation Approaches

source.note: Re-implemented from the behaviour of these files; no code from the framework is included

from_source: TopPop: item score = number of interactions of the item in URM_train (np.ediff1d of the CSC indptr)
ItemKNN cosine: w_ij = x_i . x_j / (||x_i|| ||x_j|| + shrink + 1e-6), diagonal set to 0
For every target item (column) keep the topK largest non-zero weights
Score of user u = URM_train[u] @ W
Defaults of ItemKNNCFRecommender.fit: topK 50, shrink 100, cosine, normalize True, feature_weighting none
Search ranges in run_parameter_search: topK in [5, 1000], shrink in [0, 1000]
local_choices: URM_train holds the H30 positives (train_y > 0) as binary entries
Search is a fixed grid of 8 topK x 7 shrink values over the same ranges, chosen by validation NDCG@5, instead of 35 Bayesian trials
Only cosine similarity with normalize True and no feature weighting is searched
The existing Popularity diagnostic (log of all exposures) is kept separately; TopPop counts positives only
